facts: The principal question of law arises for consideration in Appeal No. 276 of 1993 [arising out of SLP (Crl.) No. 986 of 1992], which shall reflect on Appeal No. 277 of 1993 [arising out of SLP (Crl.) No. 987 of 1992], filed by the State of Maharashtra against the judgment and order of the Bombay High Court, affirming the order of the trial Judge discharging the accused.
The accused was discharged by the trial Judge, mainly, due to technical defects and the decision was rendered as a preliminary issue on direction of the High Court.

A complaint was filed, against him after obtaining permission, u/s. 3(1)(c), read with Sections 9, 6(2)(a) and 6(2)(b) of the O.S. Act and Ss. 24(1)(d) read with 18(2) and 24(2)(d) read with S. 19(b) of the A.E. Act before the Metropolitan Magistrate.
The trial Judge turned down the plea by order dated February 24/27, 1989 and fixed date for framing the charge.
A revision, against this order, was dismissed by the High Court, on June 6, 1989.
The accused however invoked inherent jurisdiction of the High Court seeking review of the order dated June 6, 1989.
This provided an occasion to the accused for starting proceedings, afresh, for this discharge and claim in the alternative to frame charge u/s. 5 of O.S. Act instead of under Section 3.
The application was allowed by the trial Judge on January 15, 1990, and the charges under A.E. Act were dropped.
The High Court did not find any substance in it but it directed the ASJ by its order dated March 24, 1991 to decide if sanction under sections of O.S. Act and A.E. Act was in accordance with law.
issues: If the absence of sanction, by the appropriate authority, u/s. 197 Code of Criminal Procedure for prosecuting a retired public servant, vitiates the proceedings
court_reasoning: The section falls in the chapter dealing with conditions requisite for initiation of proceedings.
That is if the condition mentioned are not made out or are absent then no prosecution can be set in motion.

For instance no prosecution can be initiated in a Court of Sessions under Section 193, as it cannot take cognizance, as a court of original jurisdiction, of any offence unless the case has been committed to it by a Magistrate or the Code expressly provides for it.

And the jurisdiction of a Magistrate to take cognizance of any offence is provided by S. 190 of the Code, either on receipt of a complaint, or upon a police report or upon information received from any person other than police officer, or upon his knowledge that such offence has been committed.
holding: The High Court did not find any substance in it but it directed the ASJ by its order dated March 24, 1991 to decide if sanction under sections of O.S. Act and A.E. Act was in accordance with law.

It was held that the authorisation for institution of prosecution, for offences allegedly committed under either statute, was invalid as even though authorisation was issued, in favour of the Prosecuting Inspector who was the investigating officer, but it having been issued by an authority other than the Central Government it was not in accordance with law.

On the question of sanction u/s. 197 of the Code the High Court agreed with the ASJ that the charges itself indicated that the offences were committed during the period the accused was a serving officer, therefore, in absence of the sanction no cognizance of any of the offences could have been taken
